docs.title: About this project
docs.text:
IEEE RAS AI & Robotics Knowledge Base is a proposed documentation and learning initiative for the AI & Robotics team.

The goal is to combine onboarding, educational materials, and repeatable project documentation in a single maintainable platform.

Prototype status: This website is an initial demonstration and does not claim to be an officially published IEEE RAS resource until approved by the relevant team.

docs.title: Contact and ownership
docs.text: Team contact and maintainer details will be added after roles are confirmed.

docs.title: Contribute to the Knowledge Base
docs.text:
Everyone can improve the knowledge base, subject to team review.

  1. Create or claim a GitHub Issue describing your change.
  2. Create a feature branch from main.
  3. Edit the relevant Markdown page and test your code samples.
  4. Run python -m mkdocs build --strict locally.
  5. Open a Pull Request, complete the checklist, and request review.
  6. Merge after review and passing checks.

docs.title: Content standards
docs.text:
• Explain the objective and prerequisites.
  • Prefer short, runnable examples over unsupported claims.
  • Cite authoritative references and verify external links.
  • Label unverified project information as Pending.
  • Never commit passwords, API keys, private member data, or confidential files.
  • Respect software licenses and image rights.

See CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository for more information.

docs.title: 🎓 Learning Hub
docs.text:
Learn practical skills step by step, then apply them to team projects.

Track Level Outcome Getting Started Beginner Prepare your development environment Git & GitHub Beginner Collaborate using branches and Pull Requests Python Basics Beginner Write and run Python programs AI Roadmap Beginner → Advanced Plan your next technical milestones

Suggested order: Getting Started → Git & GitHub → Python Basics → AI Roadmap → Project Hub.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Foundations
docs.text:
Python basics, Git & GitHub, basic algebra, working with data.

Deliverable: A small Python program and your first Pull Request.

docs.title: Stage 2 — Machine Learning
docs.text:
Datasets, train/test split, classification, evaluation metrics, and scikit-learn.

Deliverable: A documented classifier with evaluation results.

docs.title: Stage 3 — Computer Vision
docs.text:
Image processing, OpenCV, camera calibration, object detection.

Deliverable: A simple object-tracking demo.

docs.title: Stage 4 — Robotics AI
docs.text:
Sensors, motion control, ROS 2 concepts, perception and decision-making.

Deliverable: A team-reviewed robotics integration project.

Keep it practical

Every learning track should link to at least one hands-on exercise or documented project.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Install Python, Git, and VS Code.

Open a terminal and verify:

python --version
git --version

On Windows, py --version may work if python --version does not.

docs.title: Your first contribution
docs.text:
1. Read Git & GitHub.
  2. Pick an open documentation Issue.
  3. Create a branch and edit a Markdown page.
  4. Open a Pull Request and request review.

Checkpoint: You can open a terminal, run Python, and explain what a Pull Request is.

docs.title: Git & GitHub
docs.text: Goal: Track changes and collaborate safely.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• Repository: project files and their history.
  • Commit: a recorded change.
  • Branch: an isolated line of work.
  • Pull Request (PR): a proposed change for review.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/OWNER/IEEE-RAS-AI-Knowledge-Base.git
cd IEEE-RAS-AI-Knowledge-Base
git checkout -b docs/my-first-update
# Edit a documentation file
git add .
git commit -m "docs: improve introduction"
git push -u origin docs/my-first-update

Replace OWNER with the actual GitHub user or organization. Open a PR from your branch into main.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text:
Create a branch named docs/your-name, add one helpful sentence to a tutorial, and submit it for review.

Checkpoint: Explain why team members should not push directly to main.

docs.title: Python Basics
docs.text: Goal: Understand variables, conditions, loops, and functions.

docs.title: 1. Variables
docs.text:
robot_name = "Sumo Bot"
battery_voltage = 7.4
is_ready = True
print(robot_name, battery_voltage, is_ready)

docs.title: 2. Conditions
docs.text:
distance_cm = 18
if distance_cm < 20:
    print("Object detected")
else:
    print("No object nearby")

docs.title: 3. Loops
docs.text:
for step in range(3):
    print("Testing step", step + 1)

docs.title: 4. Functions
docs.text:
def is_object_near(distance_cm, threshold_cm=20):
    return distance_cm < threshold_cm

assert is_object_near(10) is True
assert is_object_near(30) is False

Simulation only

The code above demonstrates Python concepts; it is not code for controlling the team's actual robot.

docs.title: Exercise
docs.text:
Write a function that returns "STOP" when distance is below 10 cm and "MOVE" otherwise. Test it with 5 cm and 20 cm.

Checkpoint: You can explain a function's input and return value.

docs.title: 🤖 Projects Hub
docs.text:
A central place to understand, reproduce, and improve team robotics projects.

Project Status Documentation Sumo Robot Documentation draft View project Future projects To be selected Use the template

Status definitions

Documentation draft means the page is a starting structure, not proof that the robot was built or tested with the listed configuration.

Each project should include a verified bill of materials, software dependencies, wiring, source code links, reproducible setup, and test results.

docs.text:

  2. Link the actual source code repository.
  3. Document board settings, dependencies, and pin assignments.
  4. Record upload procedure and safe test conditions.

Safety

Test motors with wheels lifted or the robot secured first. Verify battery polarity and current limits before powered operation.

docs.title: Project Documentation Template
docs.text:
Copy the following outline when adding a new project.

# Project Name

## Overview
What problem does it solve?

## Team & Status
Owner, contributors, last review date, current state.

## Hardware
Exact component names, specifications, bill of materials.

## Software
Languages, versions, dependencies, code repository.

## Architecture & Wiring
System diagram, pinout, connection details.

## Setup
Reproducible step-by-step instructions.

## Testing & Results
Test procedure, expected and observed results, evidence.

## Known Issues & Future Work
Limitations, planned improvements.

## References
Official manuals, source repositories, external citations.
